about: What each person reported for each check by hand, with evidence, traced to the story's criteria. ISR writes down what the person says. It never decides whether a check passed or failed.
title: ^# Hand check results: (.+)$

fields.label: Story
fields.message: Write "- Story: " and the story's file, from this file's folder.

fields.label: Script
fields.message: Write "- Script: " and the script's file, from this file's folder.

fields.label: Review
fields.message: Write "- Review: " and the script review's file, from this file's folder.

statement: ISR wrote down what each tester reported. It never decides whether a check passed or failed, and it does not accept the change.

sections.heading: Not checked by hand
sections.itemMessage: Each line reads "Criterion N: " and where the script put it, like "Criterion 1: the script lists it as already verified."

fields.label: Covers
fields.message: the check's Covers line, as the script has it

fields.label: Checked by
fields.message: who checked it and the date, like "Dana Ruiz, 2026-10-09"

fields.label: Did
fields.message: what the tester did, in their words

fields.label: Saw
fields.message: what the tester saw, in their words

fields.label: Evidence
fields.message: links or file paths, joined by "; "

fields.label: Tester says
fields.message: one of the phrases the template lists, ending with a period

outcomes.phrase: did not match what the script expects

messages.checkField: Check {n} is missing "{label}", or it is out of order. Each check has, in order: {order}.
messages.checkNumber: Number the checks as the script does: expected "### {expected}."
messages.notInScript: The script has no check {n} to report on. Each check here is one of the script's checks by hand, by its number.
messages.scriptTitle: Check {n} is "{title}" in the script. Use the script's title, word for word.
messages.scriptCovers: Check {n}'s Covers line differs from the script's. Copy it word for word: "{covers}".
messages.missingCheck: The script's check {n}, "{title}", has no entry. Record what the tester reports for it, or "Tester says: did not run it."
messages.outcome: "Tester says:" takes one of these, as the tester said it: {phrases}. If the tester didn't say, ask; never decide it for them.
messages.evidencePart: Each piece of evidence is a link or a file path, joined by "; ", with what it shows in parentheses if needed, like "evidence/stockroom-history.png (the subscriber's history in Stockroom)".
messages.evidenceNone: "{outcome}" needs evidence: links or file paths. "None." is for a check that was not finished or not run.
messages.notApproved: The review says the script is not approved for use, so no check should be run from it yet.
messages.reviewLater: The review is dated {reviewed}, after this check on {checked}. A person reviews the script before anyone uses it.
messages.reviewOther: The review is of another script. It must name the same script as this file.
messages.storyNotReady: The story it names is not ready to build from, so it has no criteria to trace to.
messages.coverageMissing: Criterion {n} is missing. Every criterion in the story appears once: under a check's Covers, or under Not checked by hand.
messages.coverageDuplicate: Criterion {n} appears more than once. It belongs in one place only.
messages.coverageUnknown: The story has no criterion {n}; it has {count}.
